t: The Mughal Empire was founded by the Timurid prince Babur in 1526 and came to rule most of the Indian subcontinent.
Akbar's cash revenue system, ranked nobility and religious accommodation built one of the largest economies of its age.
Aurangzeb's costly wars, regional revolts and the rise of the East India Company hollowed it out before its end in 1858.
dyk: Babur descended from Timur on his father's side and from Genghis Khan on his mother's, and his dynasty's name comes from the Persian word for Mongol.
ev: Babur defeats Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat and founds the empire
Babur defeats the Rajput confederacy of Rana Sanga at Khanwa
Humayun recovers Delhi after years of exile under Sher Shah Suri's rule
Akbar begins his reign, turning a fragile conquest into a stable empire
Akbar abolishes the jizya tax on non-Muslims
Aurangzeb annexes Golconda, bringing the empire near its greatest extent
Nader Shah of Persia sacks Delhi and carries off the Peacock Throne
The British exile Bahadur Shah II, the last emperor, to Rangoon
